newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - April 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a model for change which the Federal Government, analysing the Mansfield report into the ABC and looking for ways to save, may find attractive, BBC Worldwide is embracing a radical restructuring which involves turning itself into a hybrid commercial broadcaster. Its new BBC Resources division is to become a limited liability company, hiring out the BBC's production services to commercial production houses. Page 1.

The new president of the National Competition Council, Graeme Samuel, told a Melbourne conference yesterday State and Territory Governments must allocate more priority to implementing gas reform or risk losing their first competition bonus from the Federa Government. Page 3.

According to the annual Commonwealth Economic Advisory Service of Australia report, there was only a marginal rise in advertising spending in 1996, with advertisers spending A$6.8 billion in the 12 months, an increase of just 1.9 per cent on the previous year. However there are signs of a more positive year in 1997 as advertisers pour additional funds into promotions. Page 3.

In a move aimed at alleviating the mounting political damage for the Federal Government over Independent Senator Mal Colston's alleged travel rorts, Prime Minister John Howard announced yesterday he would negate the vote of Colston, leaving Independent Tasmanian Senator Brian Harradine with the balance of power in the Senate. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a move dismissed by Opposition parties as a "sham", Prime Minister John Howard declared yesterday that the Federal Government would no longer accept the vote of embattled Queensland Independent Senator Mal Colston. The move, announced on Brisbane ABC radio, comes amid mounting public anger over the Colston affair. Page 1.

As Aboriginal leaders maintained their opposition to any extinguishment of native title, Prime Minister John Howard declared yesterday that more than 75 per cent of Australia could be open to native title claims. Howard's comments are a strong indication hat the Coalition's response to the Wik ruling will be tough. Page 1.

In what is probably the biggest mistake in Australian financial history, a multi-million computer glitch at the Commonwealth Bank caused it to double all credits and debits to 300,000 accounts yesterday. According to a spokesman from the Bank, the error will take 24 hours to fix. Page 1.

Twelve-year-old Jarrod Dwyer was mauled to death by an American pit bull-great dane cross in Melbourne last night. The boy died at the scene from blood loss from injuries to his face and head, while the dog, owned by the boy's brother, was shot at twice by police who attended the scene before it was caught. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales Police Minister Paul Whelan moved last night to block Police Commissioner Peter Ryan's planned replacement for the notorious Special Branch, telling Ryan the decision to establish a unit like the Protective Security Response Group was a matter for the State Government not the Police Service. Page 1.

In a move which the Australian Pensioners and Superannuants' Federation says has angered older people, Colonial State Bank has become the first bank in this country to abandon the commitment to protect pensioner and retiree customers' savings fully from low interest rates. The bank has announced that, from next month, interest rates will no longer be determined by Federal Government deeming rates. Page 1.

Federal Veterans Affairs Minister Bruce Scott has announced he is unrepentant over his decision to allow "Anzac" to be used in connection with the Australia-New Zealand Super League Test match on Anzac Day. Scott made the decision under a post-World War Il law designed to protect the term from commercial exploitation. Page 1.

New South Wales Police Minister Paul Whelan announced in Parliament yesterday a two-month, New York-style "zero tolerance" blitz by police in Redfern, instigated by Police Commissioner Peter Ryan, has caused crime in the area to plummet, with robberies in the area's most notorious streets falling by 52 per cent. Page 3.
THE AGE

In revelations that have added weight to calls for an inquiry and Victorian Government assistance for former wards of the State, dozens of former Victorian wards came forward yesterday to tell how they had been physically and mentally abused in children's homes in the 1950s and '60s. Page 1.

According to former trustee and Federal councillor of the Transport Workers Union's Victorian branch Steve McGee, the Melbourne offices of Senator Robert Ray and then Senator Gareth Evans - two senior Keating Government ministers - were used for more than eight months to conduct a campaign for control of the union. Page 1.

The Victorian Department of Education has ordered an investigation into a survey of the all-boy Melbourne High School which asks students about the frequency of their sexual exploits, possession of pornography and whether they have used prostitutes. The survey's results are to be analysed for the school newspaper, Sentinel. Page 1.

Employees at the Royal Children's Hospital are being investigated by police after drawing pins were discovered in a sealed container of fried rice and vegetables delivered to the suburban Glenferrie Early Childhood Centre on April 1. The pins were discovered before the food was served. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
